scientific.name: Scientific journal figure
scientific.intent: A publication-grade evidence figure whose scientific structure, exact relationships, and calibrated uncertainty are visually primary.

rules: Use natural-width Arial lettering with no horizontal or vertical scaling.
Keep the hierarchy compact: panel letters, short local headings, body labels, and one small legend tier.
Use bold only for panel letters and concise local headings.

canvas.density: High information density with deliberate white space and no ornamental emptiness

art_direction: Aim for the finish of a carefully art-directed review-journal figure, not a generic flowchart.
Use domain-native scientific forms as the visual anchor: anatomy, cells, instruments, study geometry, or plotted evidence.
Allow restrained material or biological depth only when it clarifies form; keep labels and data optically crisp.
Use fine, consistent keylines and purposeful alignment so every mark appears intentionally placed.
selection_standard: Prefer the candidate with the clearest scientific topology and most exact local annotation.
Reject generic icons, empty decorative panels, or a diagram that could depict any topic after relabelling.

popsci.name: Premium editorial science illustration
popsci.intent: A sophisticated magazine-quality science visual with one memorable focal idea, strong narrative flow, and restrained explanatory annotation.

rules: Use natural-width Optima-style humanist sans lettering; never condense, expand, or shear it.
Keep in-image copy sparse and elegant; move explanation to the caption or deterministic overlay.
Use weight and scale sparingly so the illustration, not typography, carries the story.

canvas.density: One dominant editorial composition with supporting detail and generous breathing room

art_direction: Create premium editorial science art suitable for a serious long-form magazine, with a clear visual metaphor or scientific focal structure.
Use subtle tonal modelling, tactile material cues, and controlled depth to make the subject feel authored and specific without becoming photorealistic spectacle.
Build an eye path with scale, overlap, and negative space; do not line up equal boxes like presentation furniture.
Let one arresting scientific image carry the central claim while small annotations quietly explain it.
selection_standard: Prefer the candidate with the strongest single visual idea and the most graceful eye path.
Reject anything that resembles a corporate infographic, stock vector pack, classroom worksheet, or generic AI poster.

bullets.name: Decisive analytical brief visual
bullets.intent: A compact, high-clarity figure that can be understood in seconds while retaining exact evidence boundaries and professional finish.

rules: Use natural-width Helvetica Neue-style lettering with no geometric distortion.
Use a strong but shallow hierarchy optimized for quick scanning.
Keep labels short and render them directly as integrated typography; use deterministic overlay only after direct ImageGen text and targeted repair fail.

canvas.density: Compact and decisive with no dead zones, while preserving clear separation between findings

art_direction: Make the decision-relevant contrast visible immediately, using a crisp visual hierarchy and a small number of strong scientific marks.
Use one authored, domain-specific composition with editorial presence; clarity must not collapse into an icon-and-arrow worksheet or generic newsroom template.
Use alignment, scale, and restrained colour to separate findings; illustration must clarify the evidence rather than merely decorate it.
Generated elements should add domain specificity or explanatory value, not merely ornament a deterministic chart.
Keep line work precise and spacing optically even, with a newsroom graphics-desk level of finish.
selection_standard: Prefer the candidate that communicates the correct takeaway fastest without flattening uncertainty.
Reject busy illustration, tiny legends, weak alignment, or generic card grids.

eli5.name: Warm explanatory illustration
eli5.intent: A friendly, concrete scientific explainer that makes one difficult idea graspable through spatial storytelling without becoming childish or imprecise.

rules: Use natural-width Seravek-style humanist sans lettering; never squeeze or stretch words to fit.
Use large, short labels and comfortable line spacing.
Prefer everyday words and deterministic overlay when exact wording matters.

canvas.density: Generous breathing room around one concrete helper picture and a small number of supporting elements

art_direction: Build one warm, memorable helper picture with tangible objects, gentle dimensionality, and an immediately understandable spatial relationship.
Use soft editorial illustration, subtle paper-like texture, and friendly but accurate forms; avoid both sterile flowcharts and cartoon baby graphics.
Guide the eye through the explanation with placement and action rather than many arrows or text boxes.
Keep uncertainty visible through an unfinished path, open gap, pale boundary, or other concrete visual device that a new reader can explain back.
selection_standard: Prefer the candidate a non-specialist can understand and remember without the caption, while preserving the evidence boundary.
Reject clip art, emoji-like faces, classroom worksheet styling, or an abstract flowchart with labels swapped in.
